children: held its Capital Markets Day event in St. Louis, Missouri, during the week. One of the points of focus of management was the Beyond Beer portfolio, which targets drinking occasions where traditional beer is less relevant, from at-home entertaining to parties and culturally specific social events.

Bank of America analyst Andrea Pistacchi said the company looks to be well positioned for growth in Beyond Beer through its portfolio of six growing brands. Of note, through the premium canned-cocktail Cutwater brand, Anheuser-Busch

has become a top ten spirits player in the U.S. and the fastest-growing spirits company over the past 12 months. Even better, A-B management remains bullish on Cutwater’s growth potential despite the brand going against tougher comparisons. Looking ahead, Cutwater will be featured in the 2027 Super Bowl, which will be the brand's first appearance at the high-profile event.

The Beyond Beer portfolio also includes BeatBox, which is a bold, flavor-led RTD focused on younger legal-drinking-age consumers, particularly pre-party, festival, and nightlife settings. The Brutal Fruit brand is a fruit spritzer centered on premium, sociable occasions in South Africa and other African markets. Flying Fish is a flavored beer that lets A-B bring fruit-forward innovation to beer drinkers, beginning in South Africa and expanding internationally. BEATS, mainly in Brazil and Latin America, is a party-oriented RTD tied to music, nightlife, and Carnival culture. Finally, NÜTRL is a growing vodka seltzer brand in the U.S. and Canada.

title: Anheuser-Busch InBev is slowly becoming a major spirits force
